questions.question: Dr Ramdan wants to rent a premises for his dental practice. According to Article 1 of Law 49-16, does this law apply to his lease?
options: No, dental practices are excluded from the scope of application
Yes, because clinics and similar establishments are expressly covered
No, only retail businesses are concerned
Yes, but only if the practice employs more than 5 people
questions.explanation: Art. 1, II-3: the provisions of the law apply to buildings or premises in which clinics and similar establishments carry out their activity.

questions.question: According to Article 1, to which types of leases does Law 49-16 mainly apply?
options: Only residential leases
Leases of buildings or premises for commercial, industrial or craft use
Agricultural leases only
Leases of administrative premises
questions.explanation: Art. 1, I: the law applies to leases of buildings or premises for commercial, industrial or craft use.

questions.question: Dr Kamali is setting up in a commercial premises. According to Article 3, what is the mandatory form requirement for his lease?
options: A verbal agreement is sufficient between professionals
A written deed with a fixed date is mandatory
A simple agreement in principle is sufficient
A declaration to the town hall replaces the contract
questions.explanation: Art. 3: commercial leases must be concluded by written deed with a fixed date.

questions.question: According to Article 3, which document must be drawn up when handing over the premises to Dr Ramdan?
options: A simple receipt for handing over the keys
A descriptive inventory of the premises to serve as evidence between the parties
A certificate of good character
A certificate of electrical compliance
questions.explanation: Art. 3, para. 2: when handing over the premises, a descriptive inventory of the premises must be drawn up to serve as evidence between the parties.

questions.question: Dr Kamali has occupied his practice for 18 months. According to Article 4, is he entitled to the renewal of the lease?
options: Yes, because he has occupied the premises for more than one year
No, because he must prove continuous enjoyment for at least two years
Yes, because dentists benefit from a derogatory regime
No, because he has not paid a key money
questions.explanation: Art. 4, para. 1: the tenant benefits from the renewal of the lease when he proves continuous enjoyment of the premises for at least two years.

questions.question: According to Article 4, under what condition is Dr Ramdan exempt from the two-year duration requirement for renewal?
options: If he has been a dentist for more than 10 years
If he has paid a sum of money in consideration for the right to the lease
If he has carried out works in the premises
If he has signed a 5-year lease
questions.explanation: Art. 4, para. 2: the tenant is exempt from the duration condition if he has paid a sum of money in consideration for the right to the lease.

questions.question: According to Article 5, how are the rent and charges for Dr Kamali's premises determined?
options: The rent is set by a prefectural decree
The rent and charges are set by agreement between the parties
The rent is set by the court clerk
The rent is automatically indexed to inflation
questions.explanation: Art. 5, para. 1: the rent as well as all charges are set by agreement between the parties.

questions.question: According to Article 5, if the parties have not stipulated who bears the rental charges, what happens?
options: They are shared equally
They are considered to be included in the rent
They are borne exclusively by the owner
They are borne exclusively by the tenant
questions.explanation: Art. 5, para. 2: in the absence of a stipulation as to which party bears the charges, they are considered to be included in the rent.

questions.question: The revision of the rent for Dr Ramdan's practice is subject to which law according to Article 5?
options: Law No. 9-88 on accounting obligations
Law No. 07-03 relating to the revision of the amount of rent
Law No. 65-00 on health insurance
Law No. 49-16 itself only
questions.explanation: Art. 5, para. 3: the revision of the rent is subject to the provisions of Law No. 07-03.

questions.question: According to Article 6, what happens if Dr Kamali's landlord includes a clause contrary to the right to renewal?
options: The clause is valid if signed by both parties
The clause is null and void because any contrary stipulation is null
The clause is valid for the first 3 years
The clause is subject to court approval
questions.explanation: Art. 6: leases governed by the law only terminate by application of Article 26. Any contrary stipulation is null.

questions.question: According to Article 7, what does the termination compensation due to Dr Ramdan in the event of eviction correspond to?
options: Only the amount of the last annual rent
The loss suffered by the tenant as a result of the eviction
A flat-rate compensation of 50,000 DH
Reimbursement of moving costs only
questions.explanation: Art. 7, para. 2: the compensation corresponds to the loss suffered by the tenant as a result of the eviction.

questions.question: According to Article 7, on which elements is Dr Kamali's eviction compensation calculated?
options: Only on the value of the dental equipment
On the value of the business, works and moving costs
Only on the number of years of occupation
Only on the turnover of the last month
questions.explanation: Art. 7, para. 3: the compensation includes the value of the business, works expenses and moving costs.

questions.question: According to Article 7, what happens if a clause in the lease attempts to defeat Dr Ramdan's right to eviction compensation?
options: The clause is valid if accepted by the tenant
The clause is deemed null and void
The clause is valid for the first 5 years
The clause is subject to court validation
questions.explanation: Art. 7, para. 5: any clause or compromise likely to defeat the tenant's right to termination compensation is deemed null and void.

questions.question: According to Article 8, can Dr Ramdan lose his right to eviction compensation if he does not pay his rent?
options: No, the right to compensation is always acquired
Yes, if he has not paid within 15 days after formal notice and the amount due is equivalent to at least 3 months' rent
Yes, after a simple late payment
No, the landlord must first seize the court
questions.explanation: Art. 8, 1°: the landlord is not liable for compensation when the tenant has not paid within 15 days after formal notice, for an amount equivalent to at least 3 months.

questions.question: According to Article 8, can Dr Kamali lose his right to compensation if he transforms the premises without the landlord's consent?
options: No, if he restores the premises within 3 months
Yes, permanently without any possibility of regularization
No, the landlord must accept all transformations
Yes, but only if the works exceed 100,000 DH
questions.explanation: Art. 8, 2°: the landlord is exempt if the tenant transforms the premises, unless he restores the premises within the allotted time, in any case within a period not exceeding 3 months.

questions.question: According to Article 9, if Dr Ramdan's landlord wants to demolish and rebuild the premises, under what condition must he do so?
options: Without any particular condition
By proving ownership for one year from the date of the notice
With the agreement of the neighborhood only
By paying a deposit of 500,000 DH
questions.explanation: Art. 9, para. 1: the landlord must prove ownership for a period of at least one year from the date of the notice.

questions.question: According to Article 9, in the event of demolition-reconstruction, what provisional compensation must Dr Kamali receive?
options: Compensation equivalent to one year's rent
Compensation equivalent to three years' rent
Compensation equivalent to six months' rent
A flat-rate compensation of 100,000 DH
questions.explanation: Art. 9, para. 1: the landlord must pay a provisional compensation equivalent to three years' rent.

questions.question: According to Article 10, within what time limit must the landlord start the reconstruction after Dr Kamali's eviction?
options: Within 6 months
Within 2 months
Within one year
Within 3 months
questions.explanation: Art. 10: the landlord is required to start the reconstruction within two months from the date of eviction.

questions.question: According to Article 11, within what maximum time limit must the new premises be handed over to Dr Ramdan after eviction?
options: Within one year
Within two years
Within three years
Within five years
questions.explanation: Art. 11, para. 1: the premises must be handed over within a period not exceeding three years from the date of eviction.

questions.question: According to Article 16, in the event of extension or raising, what is the maximum duration of temporary eviction for Dr Kamali?
options: 6 months
1 year
2 years
3 years
questions.explanation: Art. 16, para. 1: the duration of temporary eviction cannot exceed one year from the date of eviction.

questions.question: According to Article 18, what document must the landlord produce to evict Dr Ramdan for demolition?
options: A simple registered letter
A valid building permit and an approved plan
A certificate from the town hall
An agreement from the neighbors
questions.explanation: Art. 18, para. 1: the landlord must produce a valid building permit and a plan approved by the competent authority.

questions.question: According to Article 24, can Dr Kamali sublet his dental practice?
options: No, subletting is always prohibited
Yes, unless otherwise stipulated in the lease contract
Yes, but only to another dentist
No, without the written consent of the landlord
questions.explanation: Art. 24, para. 1: the tenant may sublet all or part of the premises, unless otherwise stipulated.

questions.question: According to Article 25, can Dr Ramdan assign his lease without the landlord's consent?
options: No, the landlord's consent is always required
Yes, without the lessor's agreement and notwithstanding any contrary stipulation
Yes, but only with the court's agreement
No, the assignment of the lease is prohibited
questions.explanation: Art. 25, para. 1: the tenant has the right to assign the lease without the lessor's agreement and notwithstanding any contrary stipulation.

questions.question: According to Article 26, what is the eviction period for non-payment of rent?
options: 3 days
15 days
1 month
3 months
questions.explanation: Art. 26, para. 2: the period is set at 15 days when the request is based on non-payment of rent.

questions.question: According to Article 26, what is the eviction period for repossession of the premises for personal use?
options: 15 days
1 month
3 months
6 months
questions.explanation: Art. 26, para. 2: the period is set at 3 months when the request is based on a desire to repossess the premises for personal use.
